issue_context.title: Bug: Permanently delete doesn't work all the time
issue_context.body:
### Description

Currently when trying the prompt show and the permanently delete box is check after running the file/folder will disappear and Status center show it was successful. But refreshing the folder will show the file/folder again. 
Sometimes it also only delete the bottom most selected file and no the others.

### Steps To Reproduce

1. Select a file/folder
2. Shift delete
3. See prompt shown with check mark enabled
4. See file/folder looks deleted
5. Refresh folder

### Requirements

- permanently delete file/folder when checked

### Files Version

3.3.1.0

### Windows Version

10.0.22621.3374

### Log File

[debug.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/14895620/debug.log)
comments: @Josh65-2201 is this also an issue in v3.3?
I was able to reproduce it. I think its priority is urgent.

This appears to be caused by #14911.
@hez2010 can you take a look?

> This appears to be caused by #14911. @hez2010 can you take a look?

That was my thought as well, it's a substantial change so issues like this are expected. The main thing is to identify the issues as soon as possible so we can patch them before releasing to stable.

SetTags doesn't allow passing a null array to its `tags` parameter.
Note that CsWinRT with out-of-process server doesn't support passing null to an array parameter as well. 
We need to update all `SetTags(.., .., null)` to `SetTags(.., .., [])`. 

Would you like to submit a PR to update all the usage to SetTags in Files.App? @hishitetsu

> We need to update all SetTags(.., .., null) to SetTags(.., .., []).

This may need to be fixed, but I think the `SetTags` error is a different issue, as I don't see any logs when the deletion fails in my environment.
@Josh65-2201 do you know when `System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x800706F4)
` occurred?
No, I cleared the log but nothing is put in it, I have found that this is also effecting cut and recycle bin restore operations too.

> This may need to be fixed, but I think the `SetTags` error is a different issue

It's the same issue.

> as I don't see any logs when the deletion fails in my environment.

To reproduce, set a tag for a file and then delete it.

>do you know when `System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x800706F4) ` occurred?

```
System.Runtime.InteropServices.COMException (0x800706F4)
   at WinRT.ExceptionHelpers.<ThrowExceptionForHR>g__Throw|39_0(Int32 hr)
   at ABI.Files.App.Server.Database.IFileTagsDatabaseClassMethods.SetTags(IObjectReference _obj, String filePath, Nullable`1 frn, String[] tags)
   at Files.App.Utils.Storage.FileOperationsHelpers.<>c__DisplayClass17_1.<UpdateFileTagsDb>b__0()
   at Files.Shared.Extensions.SafetyExtensions.IgnoreExceptions(Action action, ILogger logger, Type exceptionToIgnore)
```

Here we are calling `ABI.Files.App.Server.Database.IFileTagsDatabaseClassMethods.SetTags` which is calling the server method `SetTags` from the client. And either the calling itself failed or `SetTags` throwing any exception from the server will lead to `COMException` on the client without any additional exception message.

Weird. The logs are not output in my environment, but surely fixing this solves the issue.
 I'll submit a PR. Thank you @hez2010!
